In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of simple genetic tests for disease susceptibility that can be used in the clinical setting for genetic counseling of dog owners.
the development of simplified and cost-effective genetic tests for immune diseases in purebred dogs.
the development of simplified approaches to identify DLA class II alleles and/or haplotypic associations with disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DLA class II genetic tests for immune diseases in dogs can be simplified and made more affordable by using alternative markers that are in strong linkage with the specific disease genotype.

DLA class II genetic risk assessment can be simplified by sequencing only the exon 2 region of the DQB1 allele, or with a limited single nucleotide polymorphic array designed to identify the breed-specific DQB allele.
a genetic test that is based on a combination of the 3 DQB1 alleles, the 3 DRB1 alleles, and the 2 DQA1 alleles is the best way to determine DLA class II risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DLA class IIB1 gene, and the DQB1-linked markers, can provide a simple and cost-effective alternative to 3- locus DLA class II genetic testing in dogs with immune disease.

DLA class II genetic tests for canine disease risk can be simplified to the point that they can be performed in a single laboratory using only a single genetic marker and/or a single PCR-based genetic typing technique.
genetic risk testing for DLA class II associated diseases in purebred dogs can be simplified and made more affordable by using alternative approaches to sequencing all 3 DLA genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genetic testing of dogs for immune disorders can be simplified by using alternative genetic markers to identify the DLA class IIB haplotypes that are associated with increased disease risk.

it is possible to simplify genetic testing of dogs for immune disorders by sequencing only the exon 2 region of the DQB1 or DLA-DRB1 gene or by using alternative genetic markers that are in strong linkage disequilibrium with the 3-loci DLA class II genotype.

genetic testing for canine immune diseases in some breeds may be simplified by using alternative genetic markers in strong linkage with the disease genotype, such as simple tandem repeats or small single nucleotide arrays.
